# Pandamonium v1.0.66

This train fixes the operator-reported plugin install failure on v1.0.65: repositories whose `SKILL.md` files use standard YAML folded descriptions (`description: >`) scanned successfully but never reached the install approval step. The frontmatter parser now understands folded and literal block scalars, common hyphenated publisher metadata is accepted, the scanner admits exactly the skills the installer will accept, and every reachable extension error family renders actionable copy instead of the generic setup fallback.

## MAD-953 — Extensions: install preview fails on valid SKILL.md frontmatter with YAML block scalars

### Problem

Scanning a real plugin repository such as `github.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail` succeeded on v1.0.65, but **Install plugin…** always showed the generic `Install preview unavailable: Something went wrong during setup. Check the connection and try again.` All six ponytail skills write their description as a YAML folded block scalar (`description: >`). The install-time skill adapter's hand-rolled frontmatter scan only accepted single-line scalars and `- item` list continuations, so every block-scalar continuation line raised `extension_skill_frontmatter_malformed` before approval. That code was not in the shared setup error map, so the operator saw a dead end instead of a reason. The static scanner also used a looser validator than the installer, which is why unimportable skills could pass scan and only fail at install.

### Implementation

`parse_frontmatter` in `services/memory/skill_format.py` now folds `>` block scalars (paragraph breaks preserved, newlines collapsed inside paragraphs) and keeps `|` literal scalars; double-quoted values round-trip through `json.loads` so multiline descriptions survive the markdown write/read cycle. Hyphenated keys such as `argument-hint` and `allowed-tools` parse. `SkillBundleAdapter.validate_skill_document` accepts those keys as ignored publisher metadata — authority-relevant fields such as `owner` still fail closed — and tolerates block-scalar continuation lines. The static scanner (`src/extension_scan.py`) now admits skills through that same validator, so the reviewed draft only ever contains skills the installer can admit; unimportable skills are listed in the `skill-assets-excluded` finding instead. `static/js/setupUi.js` gains per-family actionable copy for the skill, git/checkout, MCP, manifest, plugin, scan, inventory, marketplace, registry/capability/runtime, adapter, entrypoint, root, rollback, upgrade, plan, lifecycle, owner-scope, and id/signed-manifest families, with exact-code messages taking precedence, and a node contract test asserts every backend error code resolves to non-fallback copy. Feature commit `1b4e3ec4`, PR #251.

### Product value and UI visibility

Operators can paste and install any repository that ships standard-conformant skills: the scan result, approval preview, and install all agree, and the imported skills carry their full descriptions. When a repository is still rejected, the Plugins surface now names the family of failure and the next step instead of hiding it behind generic copy.

### Verification

Red-first tests: `tests/test_skill_format.py` (folded, literal, hyphenated metadata, round-trip), `tests/test_extension_skill_bundle.py` (folded description installs with its real text; publisher metadata accepted), `tests/test_extension_scan.py` (draft includes folded skills and excludes validator-rejected ones), and the `tests/test_setup_ui.js` node contract over all backend codes. Real-repo check against `github.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail` revision `e3ba2aa6`: scan drafts all six skills with no exclusions, the install preview reaches `approval_required` with `manifest_origin=scan_draft`, approve executes and installs all six, and the stored `ponytail` description is the full 825-character folded text. Full Python suite 6398 passed / 5 skipped; full Chromium suite 180 passed; CI green at merge.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency, no schema or manifest change, no database change. The parser still accepts only the bounded YAML subset used by skills; nested maps and anchors remain unsupported. Publisher fields are ignored, never enforced: Pandamonium authority still comes only from the reviewed extension manifest. Repositories with unimportable skills may now draft a subset instead of all skills, and the scan finding names the excluded skill directories.
